conditions_observed.wave_size: Overhead — surfable size for Roman

vs_forecast.comment: Spinks' call of 'hit the points' is 100% correct — the points are world-class right now. Wave quality confirmed amazing. But the crowd factor makes it impractical for Roman. KEY INSIGHT: when the Superbank connects, there is no separate Rainbow takeoff zone — the whole thing is one long wave from Snapper to the beach, and the crowd occupies the entire point. Rainbow is NOT a crowd escape from Snapper in these conditions.

observations.notes: CRITICAL CALIBRATION: Roman walked to Snapper/Rainbow in person. Waves are amazing — overhead, clean, long right-handers connecting the full Superbank. Size is surfable for Roman. BUT the crowd is too much — he doesn't know the etiquette for competing with a packed expert lineup, and there are so many surfers that people ride all the way through and walk back. Rainbow Bay is NOT a separate spot when the Superbank is on — it's all one connected wave. Snapper/Rainbow/Greenmount are effectively eliminated for Roman during this swell due to crowd. This is a persistent finding across all observations. Roman taking a rest day today, wants to surf Wed and Thu. Afternoon session possible if conditions change.

Future forecasts should weight observed wind station data over model when available, especially at Cabarita during big swells.

vs_forecast.comment: MAJOR CALIBRATION UPDATE: On Tue 24 the Superbank connected fully (Snapper to Kirra, one continuous wave, Rainbow was NOT a separate spot). Today the waves DON'T connect — there's a flat section after Snapper. Rainbow has its own independent takeoff zone with fresh waves flowing in. This means Rainbow viability depends on whether the Superbank is connecting on a given day, not just swell size/direction.

observations.notes: CRITICAL NEW INTEL: Rainbow Bay is a viable option TODAY because the Superbank is not connecting. Flat section between Snapper and Rainbow means Rainbow has its own waves, its own takeoff zone, and is not just part of the Snapper crowd riding through. Very crowded but plenty of waves. Roman scouted the paddle-out yesterday (Tue 24) so he knows where to enter. This reverses the Tue 24 observation that eliminated Rainbow. KEY LEARNING: Rainbow viability is binary — when Superbank connects (big swell, right conditions) it's NOT a separate spot. When it doesn't connect (today), it IS a separate spot with its own waves. Future forecasts need to assess Superbank connectivity, not just lump Rainbow with Snapper.

Either the evening session caught a pulse/set window the model averaged out, or the 6pm slot underestimates the actual conditions at that time. Future pattern matching should account for this model blind spot at São Pedro.

observations.notes: CRITICAL SPOT INTEL: Bafureira is an A-frame break near São Pedro do Estoril. It is extremely tide-sensitive — only surfable at mid tide due to rocks. At low tide the rocks are exposed and it's unsurfable. This is a hard constraint, not a preference. Not currently in the spot database — should be added as a lisbon-coast spot with a strict mid-tide-only window. Future forecasts must check tide state before recommending Bafureira.

This is the third observation confirming São Pedro consistently delivers bigger waves than LOTUS predicts. The 49% consistency number was spot-on though — Roman reported lots of waiting between sets. FAIR rating undersells the experience again, but the inconsistency and fatness dragged this session down compared to previous ones.

observations.notes: Session at the main peak right-hander at São Pedro. Good size but super fat and inconsistent — lots of waiting. Roman thinks they should have gone to the Bafureira A-frame instead, but it was too high tide at the start of the session. By the time they got out (9:15am), the A-frame looked much better as tide dropped towards mid. CALIBRATION: São Pedro main peak fatness is a persistent trait across ALL observations now. The spot needs either (a) decent size to compensate for the fat walls, or (b) lower/mid tide to add some punch. High tide + fat = gutless. Roman also notes his previous Sunday session at this main peak was better — likely referring to the April 5 evening session (rated 6/10) which had bigger waves that compensated for the fatness. KEY LEARNING: For future São Pedro sessions, recommend arrival timed to mid-tide (not high), and always mention Bafureira A-frame as the alternative if tide timing allows.

observations.rating_scale: 1-10 (good session despite messy conditions — would definitely go back)

conditions_observed.wave_size: Good size when conditions aligned — some big fast waves, some smaller fatter ones
conditions_observed.wave_quality: Very messy overall, likely due to wind and multiple swells competing. But when things lined up, properly surfable with somewhat long walls. Inconsistent — alternating between big/fast sets and smaller/fatter lulls.
conditions_observed.swell_comment: Multiple swells creating confused conditions. Surfline confirms 3 swell trains at noon: 1m 10s W, 0.4m 12s (longer period secondary), and 0.2m 16s SSW. The mix of short-period and long-period energy explains the alternating wave character.
conditions_observed.wind_impact: Messy — Roman attributes the chop partly to wind, though Surfline only shows 7-9kph at noon. Possibly local effects or wind building through the session.

vs_forecast.comment: Surfline showed 0.6-0.9m POOR TO FAIR at noon with 109kJ and 62% consistency. The POOR TO FAIR rating fits Roman's experience of messy-but-surfable. The three swell trains (10s W, 12s secondary, 16s SSW) explain the inconsistency and alternating wave character Roman described. Size was 'good' per Roman despite the model only showing 0.6-0.9m — the multiple swells stacking occasionally produced bigger sets than the height range suggests.

observations.notes: First session at Costa da Caparica. Roman had coaching and enjoyed it despite the messy conditions. The beach break with groynes creates multiple peaks — consistent with the Surfline guide description of 'regular groynes that trap sand and help sculpt reliable sandbars.' Roman would definitely surf here again, suggesting the spot suits his level and preferences even in suboptimal conditions. CALIBRATION: Costa da Caparica is surfable and enjoyable for Roman even in messy multi-swell conditions rated POOR TO FAIR. The long beach means crowd is spread out. When multiple swells compete, the waves alternate between big/fast and small/fat — patience between sets is rewarded. KEY LEARNING: This is a good option for coaching sessions and for days when the Estoril coast spots are too fat or too small. Being south-facing and open to W/SW swells, it picks up more energy than the sheltered Estoril spots.

The 'fat' factor suggests 10s W isn't enough period for Ribeira's reef to throw properly — the reef wants 12s+ for defined bowls. The bumpiness at high tide is NEW SPOT INTEL: Ribeira at 3.0m tide has residual chop that the model doesn't capture.

observations.notes: NEW SPOT INTEL — Ribeira d'Ilhas is bumpy on high tide even when wind is near-calm. Roman reports this as 'apparently a high tide Ribeira thing'. This contradicts the assumption that wind station glass readings translate to wave-face glass. KEY CALIBRATION: For future Ribeira recommendations, time the session to the dropping tide off high (not the high itself). The reef bowls define as the tide drops — at peak high there's too much water on the reef and the shape goes fat + bumpy. Also confirms that 10s W swell at Ribeira is fat vs the 12-16s groundswell the spot really wants. A 10s 1.6m swell should probably be rated 5/10 at Ribeira in future, not 7/10 — the model numbers flatter this spot when period is short. Session ended up fun but sub-forecast expectations.

forecast_snapshot.condition_rating: POOR TO FAIR (current page rating at 3:01pm)

observations.notes: SPOT IDENTIFICATION NOTE: Roman called this 'buffereira or whatever its called, main A frame'. Prior observations (2026-04-06) established Bafureira as a SEPARATE A-frame break near São Pedro do Estoril — highly tide-sensitive (rocks exposed at low tide). User is conflating Bafureira with the São Pedro main peak. Logging as Bafureira for continuity with prior obs. Surfline proxy spot used: São Pedro do Estoril (640b9d679b6fab7dac307b39). CALIBRATION: The 'fat and slow, bigger sets powerful' character at 10s WSW swell matches exactly the 65/100 LOTUS consistency number — consistency IS the 'fat vs powerful set' dial. Future rule: if consistency is 60-70% at a São Pedro-type spot, expect this character. Roman stayed 2 hours — note the extended session duration flags that despite the fat average waves, the bigger sets made it worth the time. Also PATTERN CONFIRMED: São Pedro / Bafureira works at near-high tide provided the WSW swell has enough size to bypass the rocks issue — Bafureira at 2.8m tide has the rocks well-covered. SIGNIFICANCE: 6/10 is a respectable South Coast local session on what was otherwise a clean-tail post-block day. Forecast had today tagged as a 5/10 afternoon-Peniche or 4/10 Carcavelos-evening — Roman found a 6/10 dawn that wasn't on the dashboard. Worth flagging São Pedro / Bafureira as a legitimate 'fat-swell 10s consistency-dependent' option for the fortnightly forecast when conditions look like today.

Self-described as 'nothing worth driving a long time for' but a 'good weekend session.' KEY CALIBRATION: Confirms Caparica handles small clean weekend windows well — the local groyne-sandbar shape gives manoeuvre-able peel on sub-1m days. Pairs with the 14 Apr Caparica 6/10 obs (messy multi-swell coaching session) to bookend the spot's working range: clean small = 5-6/10 fun, messy multi-swell = 6/10 with patience. Pattern note: Saturday late-morning 11:30am-1pm window means tide influence is part of the read — likely mid-tide-falling-into-low for this date. Future forecasts: when small clean W swell + light wind, Caparica is a banked 5/10 short-drive call rather than recommending the longer Ericeira drive.

observations.vs_forecast: Thu 30 Apr was the build-up day before Fri 1 May 'THE DAY' headline. Crowd factor: the 14s WNW pulse arriving Friday meant Thursday's lineup was already pre-loaded with pre-swell scouts. KEY FORECAST IMPACT: A 'good day on paper' at Ribeira was effectively a 5/10 experience because of crowd density — wave count of 4-with-turns in 2 hours is the metric that exposes the gap between forecast quality and surfer experience. Pattern: Ribeira on the build-up day before a flagged headline event is a CROWD TRAP — the wave count drops disproportionately to the conditions improvement.
observations.notes: Roman surfed Ribeira d'Ilhas 7:20-9:20am Thu 30 Apr. 'I guess it was good but the waves were hard to read.' SUPER CROWDED. Wave count: 4 turn-able waves across 2hr session — i.e. ~1 every 30 minutes. CRITICAL CALIBRATION FOR FUTURE FORECASTS: (1) Ribeira CROWD on the day BEFORE a forecast-headline event (e.g. day-1 of a rising 14s WNW pulse) is a major experience-degrader. The forecast quality reads 'good' but the lineup is full of locals + visitors pre-positioning for the headline. (2) 'Hard to read' at Ribeira often indicates the swell is mid-build with multiple period components arriving — wave shape is inconsistent, set timing irregular. This is distinct from the 23 Apr Ribeira high-tide-bumpy obs (that was wind-station-glass + reef-bumpy at high tide — a tide-state issue). The 30 Apr 'hard to read' is a multi-period crowd/build-up issue. (3) FORWARD FORECASTING RULE: When a major Ericeira headline is forecast for day N, do NOT recommend Ribeira on day N-1 unless conditions also peak on N-1. Better to recommend Sebastião / Foz do Lizandro / São Julião on the build-up day to dodge the crowd, then commit to Ribeira / Matadouro on the actual peak day. (4) The 4-turns-in-2hr metric is the new floor for what 'crowded sub-optimal Ribeira' looks like — even when the model says it's 6-7/10, expect 5/10 experience if crowded.

If those proxy cams look bad, assume Sebastião is also bad and don't drive. RULE FOR FUTURE FORECASTS: Never write 'check the Sebastião cam' — instead write 'check Matadouro and Foz cams as Sebastião proxies; if they look textured, assume Sebastião too and skip the drive'. observations.notes: Strong calibration data point. Coach (who Roman has weekly at Ribeira) made the forecast call — said it would be cleaner than the model suggested and was right. Two big takeaways: (1) WIND CALIBRATION — SSW 22-27kph at Ribeira d'Ilhas is not the same as the same wind at the open beach breaks; the point likely sees a bit of local shelter or the morning wind hasn't fully built yet. Future forecasts should NOT auto-skip Ribeira on SSW 20-27kph wind — recommend a dawn cam check instead. This mirrors the 4 May 'wind threshold needs nuance' calibration. (2) CROWD-FILTER PATTERN — when the LOTUS rating drops to POOR TO FAIR and the wind is forecast onshore, lineup goes from typical Ribeira crowd to ~5 people. Even at a moderate 7/10 quality, having Ribeira nearly to yourself is a big upgrade vs the usual crowded 7/10 there. Roman's coach is exploiting this pattern — bearish forecast = empty Ribeira = good coaching session. Worth flagging in future forecasts: 'Forecast looks marginal but Ribeira will be empty — good coaching/learning conditions if you're willing to risk a sub-par session.' Roman got ~10 waves in 2hrs which is exceptional for Ribeira; on a normal crowded day he might catch 4-6.
